calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY / bullish: Galaxy Digital reported $79m Q3 data-center adjusted gross profit, up from $11m in Q2, in the first full quarter under the Helios phase 1 lease, with all 133 MW of critical IT load delivered to CoreWeave by end-Q2; phase 2 is fully financed and under construction (initial data hall Q2 2027) with another 830 MW of approved Helios capacity still unleased — he says that is very bullish for CoreWeave and means it does not have to fight for financing/credit space right now. Captions render Helios as 'Halo's' and CoreWeave as 'Core Weef'.

Reiterated AVOID: CoreWeave is the worked example of the AI financing risk — its 9% 2031 debt is trading at a 14.6% yield (over 15% in recent days), a distress-like level; it has about $35B of debt and $5.5B of cash at the end of the most recent quarter against expected capex of $36B in 2026, $47B next year and $51B the year after, so it must keep raising capital at a higher cost than the last tranche, and customer prepayments cannot be assumed to continue if compute becomes less scarce.

calls.thesis: CoreWeave is the worked example: at a ~15% debt yield the equity return hurdle is 20-25%, which he thinks makes its buildout unprofitable. Neocloud doom loop: Anthropic revenue growth has stalled month-on-month (~+1.8% over the past 4 weeks after +46% QoQ in Q3), corporate AI spend is being capped, and CoreWeave's 2031 debt yield has risen from ~8% in May to over 15%, so new capital is too expensive to build data centres profitably; he is not in this part of the AI trade and expects some of these stocks to keep collapsing.
